title: 4. Rising Action: Building Momentum
use_cases: Use when building narrative tension toward the climax
Implement when expanding character arcs through internal and external conflicts
Configure when adding secondary threads that enrich the main storyline
Use when hinting at future events to maintain reader interest
Implement when balancing stakes to raise reader investment
content:
This is where the story’s engine turns up, pushing toward the climax.

- Conflict Development: Internal vs external conflicts. Example: In To Kill a Mockingbird, Scout faces internal guilt and external racism.
- Escalation of Stakes: What’s at risk for characters. Example: In The Lord of the Rings, destroying the One Ring threatens all of Middle‑Earth.
- Subplots: Secondary threads that enrich main narrative. Example: The romance subplot in Pride and Prejudice adds depth to Elizabeth’s character.
- Foreshadowing& Suspense: Hints toward future events, maintaining interest. Example: In Harry Potter, the recurring mention of “the dark lord” foreshadows Voldemort’s return.
